articles.title: Scotland: What questions face Pocognoli after Slovenia defeat?
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli has much to ponder before next month's Nations League group-stage finale after a bruising home defeat by Slovenia.
articles.body:
From the high of their first win under Sebastien Pocognoli in North Macedonia to the second Hampden low of his embryonic Scotland reign.

It has been rollercoaster four-game start to the Belgian's reign as head coach.

His first international window ends not only with Scotland's hopes of topping Nations League group and winning promotion to League A left in tatters but facing a tougher draw for the next European Championship after a likely third-place finish.

Suffering back-to-back competitive home defeats for the first time in seven years left BBC Scotland pundit Andy Halliday suggesting the "period of grace" granted for any new team boss is now over.

So what are the questions facing the 39-year-old for next month's two concluding games of the Nations League campaign?

Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony

'Outfought' and 'not good enough' - Robertson on Scotland defeat

Slovenia come from behind to beat ramshackle Scotland at Hampden

Captain Andy Robertson suggested Scotland had been "outfought" while Pocognoli referenced not being strong enough in duels.

But was it as simple as that when fighting spirit is the least you expect from a footballer playing proudly for the national jersey?

For BBC Radio Scotland's pundits, it was more a case of Scotland simply being outplayed.

Former Heart of Midlothian and Rangers midfielder Halliday thought Slovenia were "really compact, really organised. Off the ball, on the ball, so energetic, so industrious, willing to run forward, willing to play forward".

Everything Scotland were not on the night.

Former Scotland midfielder Leanne Crichton added: "Slovenia effectively critiqued and analysed Scotland from last week and have played them off the park."

For former Scotland defender Willie Miller, there was an element of both.

"In many departments, they were bullied, they were schooled in certain moments," he told Sportsound.

Pocognoli has been sticking to what is believed to be his preferred formation - three central defenders with two wing-backs playing high up the park.

Initially, it appeared to have teething problems in the first half of the goalless draw in Slovenia last month before an improved second half had many enthusing at the way they pressed forward and played on the front foot.

Judgement was suspended after the 3-0 home defeat by Switzerland given the circumstances of Jack Hendry's early red card, but the plaudits returned following a convincing 2-0 win in North Macedonia.

Neither Halliday nor Crichton are big fans of a back three and the Rangers Women head coach's main concern is how open it leaves Pocognoli's side out of possession, with Slovenia having again exposed the spaces behind the wing-backs.

Halliday, though, thinks "Sebastien Pocognoli's version of a back three out of possession is fairly positive".

"A lot of the time it is actually a back four when you see the wing-back essentially jumping as a winger and the other wing-back tucking in as a full-back," he said.

"My issue is more in possession, with the lack of penetration and runs in behind. If you play that box midfield and the amount of players Scotland play centrally then you have to be able to play through the centre of the pitch."

Miller wondered whether the defenders at Scotland's disposal are comfortable playing as a back three.

"You are asking the two wing-backs to be absolutely way up the park," he said.

"For me, the three centre-backs are exposed and don't know how to play the system.

"He's had time to work with the system, but it was just all over the place. It was unbelievably poor."

Central midfield has been Scotland's main area of strength for a number of years, but the latest showing featuring Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson, John McGinn and Ryan Christie left Halliday "so deflated".

"In terms of the shape, we have nine players centrally and got so dominated in the middle of the pitch for 90 minutes," he lamented. "I can't make sense of it.

"And that's down to Slovenia's movement, creating spaces for each other, but also how disjointed we were in terms of are we going to press, are we going to sit in our shape, are we going to try shadow passes into the midfielders?

"At no point did I think we were dialled into what we were trying to do.

"Off the ball, I do think in spells we've looked good under Pocognoli, but on the ball I'm still kind of struggling to see what we're meant to be.

"Are we a team that builds through the thirds? Are we a team that plays into the space? Are we a team that loads the wider areas and crosses into the box and floods the box?"

Crichton believes "about 50% of the team is capable of dominating the opposition" but suggests "if you don't have certain profiles" in other positions, the system breaks down.

"If you are not clinical up front and not ruthlessly defending your box, you are always going to be in a dogfight," she said.

"That's where Scotland find themselves more often than not."

Miller agreed, suggesting: "We were full of enthusiasm - front-foot football. But you've got to revisit it."

There was a clamour from fans and pundits alike to squeeze Ben Gannon-Doak into the starting XI given a couple of impressive cameos.

However, Crichton believes the wing-back position is not a comfortable fit for the young Bournemouth winger.

"I could tell within 10 minutes it wasn't going to be a good night for him because his first touch wasn't there," she said.

"Outwith his cross for the goal, his contribution was very minimal. For me, to have Aaron Hickey on the bench is astonishing because he is one of the top performers as an attacking full-back."

Therein lies the dilemma. It was Gannon-Doak's cross that led to Ryan Christie's goal and the 20-year-old has in recent games been highlighted as the one source of real pace and ability to break down a defence.

As Halliday suggests: "I don't see a successful Scotland without wingers on the pitch. I don't see us creating chances otherwise."

Scotland ended the game with wingers Josh McPake and Findlay Curtis - once Gannon-Doak had been withdrawn.

Much was made of Gilmour earning his 50th cap and Robertson reaching 100 in Skopje on Saturday, but even the stalwarts were being questioned in the aftermath of the latest defeat.

"At no point were John McGinn or Ryan Christie involved in the game," lamented Halliday, who hopes Scott McTominay's return from his minor heart operation will provide that extra spark in central midfield.

Crichton pondered whether there was too much loyalty being shown "to certain players who have been there for a long time".

Angus Gunn has made the goalkeeping jersey his own since Craig Gordon wound down his career, but the spotlight is again on the recent San Jose Earthquakes signing who was criticised for two of the goals previously lost to Switzerland.

"For me, a top goalkeeper saves that first goal," Halliday suggested. "It's not right in the corner. It's not hit with a lot of pace."

It all boils down to some hard thinking for Pocognoli as he prepares for next month's final Nations League games at home to North Macedonia and in Switzerland.

"I thought coming into this camp Sebastien Pocognoli would probably need a period of grace," Halliday said.

"I think that period of grace is now over. That was as poor a Scotland performance as I can remember for a while against an opposition you are expecting us to go and beat."

Crichton believes that Pocognoli will know that, unless he starts winning, "he's going to find himself under immense pressure and he will not get time to build a team".

Miller added: "It is very early in the new manager's reign and he is bringing younger players in.

"But, at the same time, we thought he was going to come in with a system he had perfected - that was the noises coming from Pocognoli.

"The question is, where do we go from here?"

articles.title: Antony, un parón para afinar la puntería
articles.standfirst: El brasileño es el tercer jugador de la Liga que más remata... pero aún no ha marcado
articles.summary: El brasileño es el tercer jugador de la Liga que más remata... pero aún no ha marcado
articles.body: Antony está aprovechando el largo parón de selecciones para seguir trabajando con un objetivo principal entre ceja y ceja: recuperar el gol. El brasileño ha comenzado la temporada ofreciendo buenas sensaciones, con un importante despliegue físico y mucha presencia en el ataque del Betis, pero todavía sin poder celebrar un tanto después de los primeros ocho partidos oficiales. Una situación que contrasta con su insistencia ante las porterías rivales. Algo que el extremo espera corregir cuando se reanude la competición. Porque a Antony no le está faltando precisamente intentarlo. El brasileño ha realizado 32 remates en las siete primeras jornadas de LaLiga, 13 de ellos entre los tres palos. Sólo dos futbolistas de toda la competición han disparado más: Kylian Mbappé, con 41 intentos, y Lamine Yamal, con 38. El madridista y el azulgrana han marcado siete goles cada uno. Sin embargo, el jugador del Betis todavía no ha encontrado premio. Una anomalía respecto a lo que estaba acostumbrado desde su llegada. Curiosamente, el dato, lejos de reflejar una pérdida de protagonismo ofensivo respecto al pasado curso, apunta precisamente en la dirección contraria. Antony está rematando mucho más. Si se añaden los seis disparos que realizó en el estreno de Champions frente al Lille, su balance alcanza los 38 intentos en 611 minutos, 14 entre palos. Son 5,60 disparos cada 90 minutos, un registro muy importante y que sí van consonancia con sus momentos de mayor protagonismo. La comparación con la pasada temporada resulta especialmente significativa. Antony terminó su primer curso completo como verdiblanco con 14 goles y 10 asistencias en 46 partidos y cerca de 3.500 minutos. Entonces realizó 127 disparos entre todas las competiciones, a una media de 3,28 cada 90 minutos. Ahora está en 5,60. Es decir, su frecuencia de remate ha aumentado alrededor de un 70 por ciento respecto al Antony que terminó alcanzando los 14 tantos. Incluso está encontrando portería con regularidad porque 13 de sus 32 disparos ligueros, algo más del 40 por ciento, han ido entre los tres palos. En este apartado también figura entre los mejores de LaLiga: sólo Mbappé, Raphinha y Lamine Yamal acumulan más remates a portería. El ejemplo más evidente llegó frente al Getafe en La Cartuja. Antony terminó aquel encuentro con nueve disparos, cuatro de ellos a portería, su mayor producción ofensiva de la temporada. Frente al Villarreal, pese a disputar únicamente 25 minutos, realizó otros cuatro, tres entre palos. Son cifras que muestran a un futbolista permanentemente dispuesto a buscar el gol aunque por ahora la efectividad no le haya acompañado. El parón ha permitido además a Antony continuar con el plan físico que puso en marcha este verano. El brasileño modificó su preparación individual y comenzó a trabajar con Fran Silva, especialista con el que también se ejercitan por las tardes dos de sus compañeros, Nelson Deossa y Facundo Bernal, siempre de manera coordinada con los responsables físicos del Betis. El cambio resulta visible. Antony ha ganado musculatura y ha introducido trabajo complementario dirigido especialmente a mejorar su fuerza, potencia y velocidad. "Todos me dicen que estoy más fuerte", reconocía recientemente el propio futbolista, uno de los jugadores que más tiempo dedica diariamente a su preparación. Una evolución física que tiene también como objetivo dejar definitivamente atrás los problemas de pubis que le lastraron buena parte de la pasada temporada. Antony llegó a explicar que comenzó a sufrir molestias en diciembre y terminó el curso tomando medicación para poder jugar. Hubo incluso partidos después de los cuales, según reconoció, apenas podía caminar al día siguiente. Pese a esas limitaciones, cerró la temporada con esos 14 goles y 10 asistencias. Ahora ha podido completar una pretemporada normal, trabaja sin aquellas limitaciones, y se encuentra físicamente en mejores condiciones. Le queda trasladar esa mejoría al apartado donde todavía aparece un cero. Y oportunidades no le están faltando... más aún tras la marcha de Pablo García, su principal competencia en el puesto a la espera de que lleguen más opciones para Morante. Pellegrini mantiene intacta su confianza en él y Antony ha participado en los ocho encuentros oficiales disputados hasta ahora por el Betis, siete como titular, acumulando 611 minutos. Su peso ofensivo tampoco ha disminuido: nadie en la plantilla verdiblanca se aproxima a sus 38 remates entre Liga y Champions. Después de varias semanas sin competición y sin compromisos internacionales, Antony afronta ahora un calendario cargado en el que el Betis necesitará recuperar también su producción goleadora. Los números indican que está llegando y que está disparando incluso bastante más que cuando marcaba. El siguiente paso parece evidente: afinar la puntería.

articles.title: "¿Que se va a plegar Jorge Jesús a Cristiano Ronaldo? No le conocen"
articles.standfirst: Antonio Sanz reflexiona en La Tribu sobre todo lo que ha acontecido con el futbolista portugués durante este parón y su marcha de la selección
articles.summary: Antonio Sanz reflexiona en La Tribu sobre todo lo que ha acontecido con el futbolista portugués durante este parón y su marcha de la selección
articles.body: Irene Junquera, Antonio Sanz, Ricardo Reyes, José Luis Sánchez, Fernando Kallás y David Bernabéu han sido los tertulianos de este miércoles en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por la victoria de la selección española ante Croacia, el adiós de Messi a la selección argentina y la carta de Cristiano Ronaldo. Irene Junquera. "Para que Cristiano tome una decisión tan equivocada e impulsiva como dejar la concentración tiene que tener un motivo de peso y a mí sí me cuadra lo que él dice. Cristiano se ha caracterizado por no tener filtro, por eso le creo". Antonio Sanz. "Yo era consciente de que el ego de Cristiano Ronaldo no tenía freno, pero lo que tiene es acelerador. Cristiano ha salido mal de todos los sitios: de su primera etapa en Manchester, del Real Madrid, de la Juventus, de la segunda etapa del Manchester United y de Portugal. Cristiano no escucha a nadie y ese es un gran defecto porque alguien le tiene que decir que se está equivocando. Su tiempo en la selección terminó y ya lo estiró mucho con Roberto Martínez al que prácticamente maniató en sus alineaciones. ¿Que se va a plegar Jorge Jesús a Cristiano Ronaldo? No conocen a Jorge Jesús". Ricardo Reyes. "He leído las explicaciones de Cristiano y sigo reafirmándome en que cometió un error. Por mucho que se explique no justifica lo que hizo. Yo no me imagino a Jorge Jesús empezando la rueda de prensa leyendo los ocho puntos que le redactan". José Luis Sánchez. "Lo de Cristiano se ha gestionado mal desde el final del Mundial. Me da la sensación de que el seleccionador y el presidente de la Federación no querían a Cristiano en la selección. Creo que Cristiano se equivoca marchándose del hotel. Cristiano tendría que irse con todos los honores de Portugal, cambió su historia. Antes de Cristiano Portugal era una cosa y después de Cristiano Portugal es otra.". Fernando Kallás. "Me parece delirante la carta de Cristiano Ronaldo. Solo refuerza que esto es un berrinche. Jorge Jesús habla a su manera de todos esos puntos que están ahí". David Bernabéu. "No entiendo como Jorge Jesús no se levantó en esa reunión. No recuerdo ningún futbolista, por muy grande que sea, que le haya dicho a un seleccionador o a un entrenador lo que tiene que decir delante de un micrófono".

articles.title: Unai Simón sigue defendiendo el mejor currículum del mundo
articles.standfirst: Espectacular actuación del portero en Split
articles.summary: Espectacular actuación del portero en Split
articles.body: El MVP es para Merino, que anotó los dos goles de la remontada, pero si España aguantó de pie y llegó al minuto 88 con opciones de ganar el partido fue gracias a Unai Simón, que firmó una actuación memorable. Tres paradones para reivindicarse, una vez más, como el portero titular de la selección —no hay debate posible— y como uno de los mejores porteros del mundo. El jugador con la mejor racha de imbatibilidad de la historia de los mundiales empezó su recital en la primera parte con un paradón a Perisic, que acertaría en la segunda ocasión que tuvo pero tras otra intervención milagrosa de Unai, que había sacado el remate de gol de Matanovic. Unai lo paraba todo y hasta arreglaba los problemas que ellos mismos se creaban. “Una de ellas viene por una mala salida mía, que se la doy a Laporte, pero para eso estamos, para solucionar cosas”, admitía Unai, siempre quitándose mérito. “Una lástima ese gol encajado, pero el hombre del partido es Merino, porque salir de esa manera y meter dos goles...”, insistía el portero de la selección. La segunda parte también tuvo el milagro de Unai, con un paradón con el pie a Perisic tras un fallo de Zubimendi. Posiblemente, la mejor parada de la noche. “Croacia juega en su casa, viene de hacer un partido que es un poco flojo por su parte y quieren demostrar a su afición que aprietan al hombre. No todo va a ser un camino de rosas pero tenemos que seguir con esta ambición de querer ganar todos los partidos, que no nos valen los empates”, dijo Unai, que recibió tras el encuentro la felicitación de De la Fuente, que había celebrado como goles las paradas de Unai. Campeón de la Nations League en 2023, de la Eurocopa en 2024 y del Mundial en 2026, salió de la última Copa del Mundo con el Guante de Oro, siete porterías a cero en ocho partidos y un solo gol encajado. Además, fijó en 649 minutos la mejor racha de imbatibilidad de la historia de los Mundiales. Un currículum que explica la confianza absoluta del entrenador y que Unai sigue defendiendo pese a la presión de Raya y Joan García con actuaciones memorables como la de Split.

articles.title: Los cracks despiden a Messi: "El mejor de la historia, extraterrestre"
articles.standfirst: Ronaldinho, Neymar, Modric y otros jugadores elogian a Leo en su adiós a la selección
articles.summary: Ronaldinho, Neymar, Modric y otros jugadores elogian a Leo en su adiós a la selección
articles.body: Messi puso punto y final a su andadura en la selección. Atrás deja títulos, goles y actuaciones memorables y por delante genera un vacío que será complicado de llenar en la Albiceleste. Nada más terminar el encuentro ante Benín, el último con su combinado nacional, se sucedieron los elogios hacia él. A Leo le llegaron bonitas palabras tanto de compañeros como de rivales. Ronaldinho dejó uno de los mensajes más emotivos. "¡Qué placer y qué alegría haber formado parte de tu historia desde el primer día, hermano! Nos hiciste sonreír y disfrutar tanto del fútbol... Tu nombre está en la historia de tu país, de todo el mundo. Solo nosotros sabemos la alegría que sentimos al cumplir nuestro sueño de infancia, representar a toda nuestra nación y ser campeones del mundo. Lo diste todo por tu selección y por tu país. Te entiendo perfectamente y sé que todo lo relacionado con la familia nos hace replantearnos las cosas. Disfruta de la vida, hermano. Te deseo lo mejor, hoy y siempre", escribió en 'X'. Neymar también se sumó al homenaje público. "Quien ama el fútbol te aprovechó a lo largo de estos años… Hoy es tu último partido con la camiseta de tu selección, de tu país y espero que disfrutes cada segundo, que todos los homenajes de hoy te hagan feliz. No es solo Argentina la que te agradece, el mundo te agradece por todo lo que hiciste por el fútbol. Gracias por hacerme amar aún más el fútbol, fue un honor haber jugado contra ti y más aún hacer historia a tu lado. Gracias, Leo Messi", publicó en sus redes sociales. Modric se refirió al adiós de Leo tras el encuentro de Croacia ante España. "¿Qué decir de Messi? Es una pena que se despida de su selección, pero es su decisión y hay que respetarlo. Ganó el Mundial que quería, es uno de los mejores jugadores del mundo y ha sido un placer verlo jugar, aunque lo he sufrido mucho con la selección y con el Madrid. Es un futbolista único. Le deseo mucha suerte", dijo. Arturo Vidal, aunque más breve, homenajeó a Messi en Instagram. "Hoy juegas tu último partido por tu país, amigo. Te deseo lo mejor siempre. El mejor de la historia, extraterrestre". Uno de los mensajes más emotivos de sus actuales compañeros de selección fue el de Julián Alvarez. "Qué privilegio compartir cancha y tantos momentos con vos. Primero, te admiré como un nene, como millones de argentinos que crecimos soñando con ser futbolistas gracias a vos. Después, tuve la suerte de conocerte, ser tu compañero y vivir cosas que nunca voy a olvidar. Gracias por todo lo que nos diste, por representar a nuestro país de la manera que lo hiciste y por dejarnos un legado que va mucho más allá del fútbol. Te vamos a extrañar mucho con la celeste y blanca. Para mí vas a ser siempre el más grande. Muchas gracias, Leo", publicó en Instagram.

articles.title: Colombia levanta cabeza y hunde a Perú en la incertidumbre
articles.standfirst: Los cafeteros cierran el parón con victoria
articles.summary: Los cafeteros cierran el parón con victoria
articles.body: La selección colombiana levantó la cabeza este martes al vencer 2-0 con goles del lateral Samuel Velásquez y del centrocampista Daniel Arcila a Perú, que se hundió en la incertidumbre tras esta fecha FIFA en la que no solo perdió, sino que no encuentra claridad. En un amistoso disputado en el Nu Stadium de la ciudad estadounidense de Miami, los cafeteros mejoraron la imagen que habían dejado en los juegos anteriores y superaron a un rival con muchos problemas que hoy dejó preocupados a sus aficionados. El primer gol llegó al 57 en una buena jugada de Gómez, que mandó un centro venenoso que despejó Gallese primero y luego Jesús Pretell y en el rebote el lateral Velásquez, sin pensarlo mucho, sacó un potente remate de zurda imposible de atajar para el guardameta peruano. El partido se hizo más difícil para la Bicolor al 65 cuando el central Miguel Araújo, que llevaba apenas dos minutos en cancha, perdió un balón en terreno propio con el atacante colombiano Camilo Durán y lo derribó antes de que entrara al área, por lo que fue expulsado por el árbitro estadounidense Rubiel Vásquez. Tras esa jugada, los peruanos jugaron mucho más atrás y el balón le llegó muy poco a los atacantes Gianluca Lapadula y André Carrillo, que quedaron aislados e incluso tuvieron que ponerse el overol para ayudar en defensa. En ese contexto, Colombia tuvo más oportunidades para ampliar la ventaja con remates del goleador Kevin Viveros, Durán y Richard Ríos, que fueron atajados por Gallese o que pasaron desviados. Al final, los cafeteros lograron ampliar al 92 en una buena jugada en la que Arcila recibió en el borde del área y sacó un potente remate que esta vez no pudo detener Gallese. Los colombianos dejaron una mejor imagen que en los dos partidos anteriores, de los cuales empataron uno con México y perdieron otro con Paraguay.

El centrocampista, que tiene una salario semanal que ronda los 295.000 euros, fue interceptado por la autoridades en abril de 2025 cerca de la ciudad deportiva del Chelsea en Cobham (Surrey). Moisés Caicedo, que fue sancionado tras comparecer el tribunal de magistrados de Crawley, se arriesga a perder el carnet de conducir. En Gran Bretaña los conductores que acumulan 12 puntos en un periodo de tres años se les prohíbe conducir durante seis meses. Las personas con permiso de conducir internacional pueden utilizarlo en Gran Bretaña durante 12 meses. Cuando el vehículo fue incautado el Chelsea restó importancia al suceso calificándolo de "asunto personal".

articles.title: Sporting director Stewart to leave Chelsea
articles.summary: Chelsea sporting director Laurence Stewart is set to leave the club by mutual consent in the near future.
articles.body:
Chelsea sporting director Laurence Stewart is set to leave the club by mutual consent in the near future.

The 40-year-old leaves on excellent terms to pursue other opportunities in a move that is internally seen as related to the "tweak of the (recruitment) model" that influential co-owner Behdad Eghbali spoke about at the end of last season.

Stewart has spent nearly four years at Chelsea under the BlueCo ownership, but many of his responsibilities will be absorbed into the roles of Joe Shields and Sam Jewell.

Shields and Jewell work closely with influential sporting director Paul Winstanley on player identification, negotiations and squad planning.

Winstanley also oversees a host of other areas, including medical, player support and other internal operations.

Meanwhile, Dave Fallows is part of the sporting leadership in a flexible advisory capacity rather than working within a fixed remit on a day-to-day basis.

It is part of the structure around Xabi Alonso, whose arrival sparked further conversations about how to improve both the squad and the way the club operates behind the scenes.

The former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen manager has spoken about wanting to be heavily involved in transfer decisions, including playing a role in the decision to sign players aged over 30 such as Jordan Henderson, Danny Welbeck and Emiliano Martinez.

There will now be a restructure below director level, with data being better integrated into decision-making and further mid-level appointments made to support the current leadership team.

Sources say this restructure is unrelated to Todd Boehly and Mark Walter selling their stakes in Chelsea for £475m each last month.

articles.title: ‘Perhaps the saddest day of my career’ – Lionel Messi says emotional farewell to Argentina
articles.summary: The GOAT admits it’s hard to say goodbye.
articles.body:
An emotional Lionel Messi addressed a packed stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday night after playing his final ever game for Argentina.

The GOAT scored in a 3-0 friendly win over Benin and couldn't hold back the tears as he spoke about his sadness at playing in Argentina's colors for the final time in his incredible career.

"I'm going to miss playing here so much. I always received tremendous affection, from beginning to end. I'm so grateful for everything I experienced. I'm thankful for all this time: wherever I was, the stadium was packed, whatever the match. They were everywhere, making a huge effort, traveling to the World Cups," he said. "We always feel like the home team everywhere we go. In this place, I experienced one of the happiest moments of my life: playing here after winning the World Cup. To this day, I watch the videos and I get emotional. It was spectacular. Thank you so much."

"I'm going to miss playing here so much. I always received tremendous affection, from beginning to end. I'm so grateful for everything I experienced. I'm thankful for all this time: wherever I was, the stadium was packed, whatever the match. They were everywhere, making a huge effort, traveling to the World Cups," he said.

"We always feel like the home team everywhere we go. In this place, I experienced one of the happiest moments of my life: playing here after winning the World Cup. To this day, I watch the videos and I get emotional. It was spectacular. Thank you so much."

Messi also went on to say the moment was "perhaps the saddest" of his career but insisted his support for the team would remain as strong as ever.

"Today is perhaps the saddest day of my career. I'll be there for them, supporting these guys and those who come after. Always united. It's been more than proven that when we're united, we can overcome anything. Tough times are coming, and we have to be there for them more than ever," he added. "To achieve great things, you have to build strong teams. There are people who want to see the national team fail, and we can't give them the satisfaction. "It's in difficult times that you see the true strength of the team. We were an extraordinary group. I've spoken more than ever, but I don't want to leave here. Thank you so much. I love you all."

"Today is perhaps the saddest day of my career. I'll be there for them, supporting these guys and those who come after. Always united. It's been more than proven that when we're united, we can overcome anything. Tough times are coming, and we have to be there for them more than ever," he added.

"To achieve great things, you have to build strong teams. There are people who want to see the national team fail, and we can't give them the satisfaction.

"It's in difficult times that you see the true strength of the team. We were an extraordinary group. I've spoken more than ever, but I don't want to leave here. Thank you so much. I love you all."

The GOAT bows out after 208 games and 126 goals for Argentina. He won the World Cup, two Copa America titles, is his country's most capped player, leading scorer and an all-time great who will simply never be forgotten.

articles.title: Early AFC stakes grow as Bills search for offensive answers
articles.summary: The Bills will be facing a Rams defense that is coming off a dominant performance against the Eagles, and should be getting back injured Aaron Donald.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK - Two games into the 2026 NFL season, the Buffalo Bills' offense was humming to the tune of 77 points, 36 of those coming against a Houston Texans defense that, at least heading into the year, was considered the most ferocious unit in the league.

Memories of 2024, when the Bills scored a franchise-record 525 points, were dancing in the heads of Bills fans who wondered if this version of the offense, led by then-offensive coordinator and now head coach Joe Brady, could challenge that mark.

Since then the Bills have tacked on 50 more points which is nothing to sneeze at, but no one - least of all Brady and Josh Allen - would consider either performance against the Los Angeles Chargers or New England Patriots impressive.

They survived five turnovers to somehow beat the Chargers, but they could not overcome two more killer turnovers and seven of 11 possessions where they made one or zero first downs in their loss to the Patriots .

"There's a standard by which we play, and we're either playing to that standard or not," Brady said, the insinuation that the standard has not been met the last two weeks. "It obviously wasn't good enough, and we didn't find a way to go 1-0."

Going 1-0 is going to be even more difficult this week when the Bills have to play the preseason Super Bowl betting favorite Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football at SoFi Stadium.

"I've always believed that great teams don't have to lose to learn, but we lost (Sunday) and it's now what are we putting out there," Brady said. "We're still learning about our football team. I think everybody in that locker room right now needs to sit there and say, 'Hey, I've got to be better. If I'm better and I worry about making myself better right now then we'll continue to improve as a football team.'"

As dynamic as the Rams ' Matthew Stafford-led offense can be, their often overlooked defense is coming off a tremendous shutdown of the Philadelphia Eagles last Sunday, granted an Eagles team playing without four offensive stars in RB Saquon Barkley, WR DeVonta Smith, OL Lane Johnson and TE Dallas Goedert.

Rams defense fuels comeback win over Eagles

On the flip side, though, the Rams did not have two of their future first-ballot Hall of Famers, edge rusher Myles Garrett who is on injured reserve, and Aaron Donald who sat out with a minor back injury, plus starting corner Jaylen Watson.

The Rams gave up 20 first-half points due in large part to a pair of Stafford interceptions and a punt coverage breakdown that gave the Eagles scoring driving starts at the Rams 28-, 17-, and 35-yard line, but thereafter the Rams obliterated Philadelphia the rest of the way.

In the second half, the Eagles managed four first downs and 72 yards and for the game, Philly had 12 first downs, 172 yards and went 1-for-16 on third- and fourth-down plays.

That domination kept the Rams in it and set the stage for Stafford-led drives of 98 and 79 yards which resulted in two TD runs by Kyren Williams in the final four minutes of the game to pull off a 24-20 victory.

"Our defense was outstanding, getting that stop a bunch of times," Stafford said. "Can't say enough good things about our defense and how resilient they played."

Rams coach Sean McVay wholeheartedly agreed, admitting that the offense and special teams made it very difficult, but the defense persevered.

"I thought our guys answered the bell," McVay said. "For them to be 1-of-16 on conversion downs, that's so big. In the spirit at which they kept competing in spite of some other things that maybe weren't going our way with the offense or in the kicking game, I think it says a lot about them but it was their ability to consistently execute.

"Somebody sent me something that at one point there was a 3% chance we win that game. But those defensive guys, they didn't give a (crap) about those chances. They kept playing and make them snap it one more time. Then the next thing you know, it leads to a stop. Offense goes 98 yards, they get another stop, offense goes 79 yards, before you know it you're taking a knee and you're like, 'Holy geez, that was awesome by the D.' They did a great job. I was really proud of them."

You would expect the Rams - who are expected to get Donald back - will get a much tougher test from Allen and the Bills, provided Buffalo gets back to playing the way it did in the first two weeks, and McVay is already gearing up for the challenge.

Sean McVay praises Bills offense ahead of Monday matchup

"I know we're playing a great offense, I know we're playing a really good football team that's complete," McVay said, though having admitted he hadn't quite delved into the film, he perhaps hasn't seen how troubled the Bills' defensive backfield is, or how mistake-prone the Bills' offense has been.

Continuing, McVay said, "Joe Brady's done a great job with their offense the last handful of years, Josh is really high level, they've added some new playmakers in DJ Moore, they have an explosive back in (James) Cook that can really make you pay. It seems like (Dalton) Kincaid has been balling and doing his thing. I've always thought (Khalil) Shakir is really one of the more underrated players in this league and (Dawson) Knox is great. They have a great offensive line, great personnel.

"It's a great football team, but I'm interested to see how we can play cleaner football. I love the way that we played defensively. How do we build on that but know that it's going to be different with what Buffalo presents compared to what we defended (last Sunday) in terms of what's required to play at a high level."

Sal Maiorana has covered the Buffalo Bills for more than four decades including 37 years as the full-time beat writer/columnist for the D&C. He has written numerous books about the history of the team, and he is also co-host of the BLEAV in Bills podcast/YouTube show. He can be reached at maiorana@gannett.com, and you can follow him on X @salmaiorana and on Bluesky @salmaiorana.bsky.social.

articles.title: "¿Cristiano? Jugué con un rey llamado Eusébio, compartí tiempo con un rey llamado Pelé, Maradona... Nunca he visto nada parecido"
articles.standfirst: António Simoes se 'moja' sobre el conflicto entre Cristiano Ronaldo y Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: António Simoes se 'moja' sobre el conflicto entre Cristiano Ronaldo y Jorge Jesus
articles.body: Sin duda, António Simoes es una voz autorizada dentro del fútbol portugués. La leyenda del Benfica es el jugador más joven de la historia en ganar la Copa de Europa (18 años y 139 días, en 1962 la ganó con los lisboetas), levantó 10 veces la liga portuguesa y fue tercero con Portugal en el Mundial de 1966. Su relación con Cristiano Ronaldo, sin embargo... es abrupta. Y en varias ocasiones ha hablado de forma crítica sobre el de Madeira. Ahora, con el conflicto latente entre CR7 y Jorge Jesus, no ha sido diferente. "Jorge Jesus tiene todo el derecho a hacer que Cristiano Ronaldo caliente durante un minuto o 30. Es el entrenador. Yo aprendí y crecí respetando a mis compañeros más veteranos y al entrenador. ¿Por qué Cristiano tiene que recibir un trato especial? Jugué con un rey llamado Eusébio. Compartí tiempo con un rey llamado Pelé, Maradona y compañía... Nunca he visto nada parecido en torno a un rey", contaba Simoes en unas declaraciones que recogen en 'A Bola'. El veterano ex futbolista, mientras, pide que las partes implicadas en la 'guerra' firmen la paz: "Es mejor que se reúnan y hagan las paces, en lugar de mantener la guerra. Esto no tiene sentido. Si se dan las condiciones para que Cristiano regrese, debería ser bienvenido, pero bienvenido por todos, no solo por unos pocos. No tenemos por qué estar de acuerdo con Cristiano, y creo que se equivoca. Ahora bien, si ha reconocido su error, démosle la oportunidad de tener, al menos, una despedida digna de su prestigio. Lo que se necesita es sentido común y tolerancia". Unas palabras que van de la mano con otras en las que pone en duda que Cristiano pueda, en 2026, ser un activo valioso para la Selección de Portugal: "Sinceramente, tengo dudas sobre si es un jugador valioso. Ser un jugador valioso implica mucho más que simplemente ser útil. Es algo que el entrenador debe gestionar y saber qué hacer con él. Si quiere jugar, no hay ningún problema. Ahora bien, también tiene que entender que quizás no juegue tanto como quisiera". Simoes recuerda que ya habló con Cris en Sudáfrica, en 2010. "A veces sentimos que solo piensa en sí mismo. Viví esta experiencia en el Mundial de Sudáfrica, y tuve la oportunidad de hablar con él. Ya en aquel momento vi una pequeña señal de que las cosas no deberían ser de esa manera", relata. 16 años después, cree que ha llegado el momento del adiós para el jugador de Madeira: "Ronaldo fue el jugador que disputó más minutos con Roberto Martínez, y eso no parece lógico. Después de marcar 1.000 goles, Cristiano Ronaldo seguirá jugando con la selección hasta los 49 años. Un hombre de 41 años que juega al fútbol... ¿no sería mejor que lo dejara?".

articles.title: Report: 16-year-old Real Madrid target wants Barcelona move ‘at all costs’
articles.summary: One of the biggest transfer sagas doing the rounds in Europe in recent weeks is the uncertain future of JJ Gabriel.The Manchester United wonderkid has expres...
articles.body:
One of the biggest transfer sagas doing the rounds in Europe in recent weeks is the uncertain future of JJ Gabriel.

The Manchester United wonderkid has expressed his desire to leave the club, and European giants have set their sights on signing him.

Now, Los Blancos could face a significant obstacle in their pursuit of the 16-year-old England starlet.

According to Diario SPORT journalist Jaume Marcet , the highly rated teenager is prioritising a move to Barcelona despite interest from elsewhere.

Gabriel wants to play for Barcelona "at all costs." He celebrated his 16th birthday just a day ago and is keen to continue his career elsewhere.

The development comes shortly after Madrid were said to be among the clubs making the strongest push for Gabriel.

Madrid and Barcelona were both very concrete in their interest, with the Spanish giants prepared to offer substantial packages involving salary, bonuses and a signing-on fee.

JJ Gabriel has asked to leave Manchester United. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Bayern Munich have also remained in the race, while PSG have been monitoring the situation in case the opportunity presents itself.

Gabriel is also expected to receive a Cypriot passport, a development that could potentially make a move to Spain easier.

A free transfer in January has been mentioned as the plan if the necessary conditions are met. However, this Barça development could change Madrid's stance.

Financial terms are one thing, but convincing a youngster whose preferred destination is reportedly Barcelona presents a different challenge.

Losing an elite prospect to Barcelona would naturally sting, particularly when Madrid have invested considerable effort in trying to sign him.

JJ Gabriel is shopping for a new club in the market. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

However, this is also where Madrid need to trust what they have built. La Fabrica is producing talent, and the club continues to identify elite youngsters across Europe.

Gabriel, for all his talent, is just getting started in his career, and there is no guarantee about how and where his development will take him.

Madrid should only try to sign players who are 100 percent committed to the club's cause, and if Gabriel is having second thoughts, Los Blancos should refrain from making a move.

It remains to be seen what the 16-year-old decides for his future and where he moves next to continue his development.

articles.title: Nico Schlotterbeck could return for Borussia Dortmund’s Champions League game
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund’s defender Nico Schlotterbeck picked up an outer ligament injury to his right ankle while training with the German national team last week....
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund's defender Nico Schlotterbeck picked up an outer ligament injury to his right ankle while training with the German national team last week. According to Sport BILD , he will most likely miss Friday's game against Werder Bremen. However, the club is confident that he will be fit again for the UEFA Champions League match at Bodø/Glimt on Wednesday.

Schlotterbeck picked up the injury during a 'fun competitive drill'. The players were dribbling around slalom poles in four groups. Schlotterbeck lost control of the ball and veered into another group, where Finn Jeltsch was dribbling at the same time – twisting his ankle and sustaining an injury.

In the summer, Schlotterbeck picked up an injury in the 2026 FIFA World Cup game against Ivory Coast and had to come off at halftime. He recently returned to the team and featured in Dortmund's two Bundesliga wins against Paderborn and Stuttgart before the international break. He also played for Germany in the 1-1 draw against the Netherlands.

articles.title: Zinedine Zidane shrugs off question of Michael Olise being the best footballer in the world
articles.summary: Zidane answered diplomatically when he was asked if Olise is the best player in the world right now.
articles.body:
All of the talk surrounding this month's Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium is centered around Barcelona and Spain's Lamine Yamal and Bayern Munich and England's Harry Kane. By all accounts, the pair of superstars are slated to be the ones duking it out for this year's prestigious honor, as voting has only recently closed. However, with the way he's carried on playing exceptionally well for Bayern and just how good he was during the international break for France, Michael Olise's name has also been in the discussion despite his less realistic chances of winning.

From France's four UEFA Nations League matches against Turkey, Belgium (twice), and Italy, Olise tallied four goals and two assists, having contributed quite literally to all but one of France's goals during the international break—which was Désiré Doué's goal in the 4-1 win over Belgium in Saint-Denis. It's even more impressive that Olise didn't even start in all of those matches, as manager Zinedine Zidane rotated his squad across the quartet of fixtures.

His contributions for Les Bleus add to the eight goals and four assists he's tallied from seven appearances so far this season for Bayern. All of that, too, comes after a World Cup where he set the record for assists at a single tournament (7). Not to mention, he bagged 22 goals and 31 assists for Bayern last season, was named the Bundesliga's Player of the Year, and came ever so close to Thomas Müller's single-season Bundesliga assists record of 21, having bagged 19 himself.

In the post-match press conference after France's 4-1, come-from-behind win over Belgium at the Stade de France to close out their international break, Zidane was asked by the press whether he feels Olise is currently the best player in the world. Ironically enough, the question was lodged at Zidane on the eve of Lionel Messi playing his last-ever match for Argentina. In an effort to perhaps stave off a slew of follow-up questions, Zidane simply replied, "I have nothing to say. What he's doing is just exceptional," while cracking a smile (via @iMiaSanMia ).

Zizou might very well believe Olise is the best player in the world right now, but having only just started his tenure as manager of the French national team, he's leaving the headline-grabbing responses for other people to give the press for the time being.

articles.title: RB Leipzig’s Christoph Baumgartner works towards comeback

articles.body:
After sustaining a thigh injury which required surgery just weeks before the 2026 FIFA World Cup, RB Leipzig's Christoph Baumgartner is working on his comeback.

On Tuesday, the Bundesliga side confirmed that the Austrian had indeed returned to team training, albeit partially. Still, it's positive news for Leipzig and Baumgartner, who scored 17 goals and provided nine assists in 37 appearances across all competitions last season.

According to a report by Kicker , it's unclear as to when Baumgartner will fully return to training, and uncertain as to when he will be available to Martin Demichelis.

Additionally, both Rocco Reitz and Brajan Gruda returned to training on Tuesday. The former suffered a muscular injury at the start of September, while Gruda was replaced after 26 minutes against Bayer Leverkusen on Matchday 4 with an abdominal injury, and subsequently had to withdraw from Jürgen Klopp's maiden Germany squad.

Demichelis' Leipzig host Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday before welcoming PSV in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday before a trip to Bayern Munich the following week.

articles.title: Ronaldo accuses coach Jesus of broken promises but leaves Portugal return open
articles.summary: Soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo has accused Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word, saying a failed agreement to publicly explain his omission against Norway drove him out of the camp but ​insisting he remained available after any punishment.
articles.body: Soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo has accused Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word, saying a failed agreement to publicly explain his omission against Norway drove him out of the camp but ​insisting he remained available after any punishment. In a lengthy statement, the 41-year-old gave his ‌account of the dispute that prompted his departure from Copenhagen before Portugal’s Nations League match versus Denmark last week. Ronaldo said Jesus had agreed a plan under which the forward would miss the Norway and Denmark matches to manage ​his fitness. However, on the day of the Norway game, the coach told him ​he would play for 30 minutes. “Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from ⁠halftime onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” Ronaldo said. “The manager had broken ​his word to me.” Portugal’s captain and all-time leading scorer said a subsequent meeting with Jesus, attended by ​his club side Al Nassr’s sporting director Simao Coutinho, produced an agreement for the coach to clarify events at his next press conference. According to Ronaldo, an eight-point document was prepared saying he had never demanded playing time, had ​respected Jesus’ decisions and that the coach asking him to warm up without bringing him on ​had been a mistake. Ronaldo said the agreed notes did not require Jesus to apologize to him but said ‌the coach’s ⁠public remarks bore no resemblance to their private discussion. “It was the second time he had broken his word to me,” Ronaldo said. “I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises.” The statement provided Ronaldo’s account but on Sunday, after Portugal’s win over Norway, Jesus denied ​he had made any agreement ​with the player ⁠but left the door open for his return. The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) did not immediately respond to a request for comment about Ronaldo’s statement. Ronaldo apologized for failing ​to greet supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his team ​mates, accepting that ⁠his captaincy made his conduct more serious. “The consequences of my actions must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation,” he said. Despite the rupture, Ronaldo said he was not limiting his international ambitions ⁠to a ​farewell appearance. “If I’m physically fit, playing for my club — ​scoring goals, I hope — after serving whatever suspension is imposed on me, I’ll be available, as I’ve always been until now, ​to compete and win for our national team,” he added.

articles.title: Florentino Perez has not given up on Bayern Munich superstar amid contract renewal talks
articles.summary: Real Madrid have not abandoned their interest in Michael Olise, with Florentino Perez continuing to monitor the Bayern Munich winger’s contract situation ahe...
articles.body:
Real Madrid have not abandoned their interest in Michael Olise, with Florentino Perez continuing to monitor the Bayern Munich winger's contract situation ahead of a possible move next summer, reports Defensa Central

It is known that Bayern are working on a new contract for Olise, but the France international is seeking a release clause as part of any extension .

That detail could be crucial for Real Madrid, who want to know whether a future exit route can be established before deciding how aggressively to pursue the winger.

For now, Olise remains comfortable in Munich and appreciates the opportunity Bayern gave him, but the possibility of moving to the Santiago Bernabeu is understood to appeal to him.

Michael Olise transfer: Real Madrid waiting on Bayern clause

As such, Bayern's renewal talks could determine whether Real Madrid have a realistic path towards signing Olise.

Real Madrid are still keeping an eye on Michael Olise. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

The German club rejected Real Madrid's interest when the Spanish giants explored a deal last summer, but the situation could change if a release clause is included in a new contract.

The aforementioned outlet claims Real Madrid could be prepared to consider a figure approaching €200 million, although that should be treated as a potential valuation rather than a confirmed offer.

Real Madrid see Olise as a potential undisputed starter

Understandably, a move of that financial scale would come with significant expectations, as Olise would not be arriving at Real Madrid just to provide squad depth.

Rather, he would be expected to become an undisputed starter, raising an obvious question about how the club would accommodate him alongside Vinicius Jr, Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande.

That competition would become even more complicated given Vinícius' long-term contract, which runs until 2032.

Olise is in talks with Bayern Munich over a new contract. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

Madrid would therefore need to decide whether Olise is viewed as a direct starter in the long term or whether the squad can realistically support another elite attacking signing.

Olise could become Real Madrid's next record signing

Real Madrid have already invested heavily in Diomande, who arrived for €125m plus €15m in potential bonuses.

If the club were to subsequently spend close to €200m on Olise, it would represent an extraordinary level of spending across two transfer windows and potentially make both players the two most expensive signings in Real Madrid history.

For now, though, all eyes are on Bayern's renewal negotiations. If Olise secures the release mechanism he wants, Real Madrid could have a much clearer route to revisit their interest next summer.

articles.title: Cole Campbell interview: United States debutant explains Elversberg move and forging his own path in Bundesliga
articles.summary: In this interview with Cole Campbell, the newest United States international discusses the influence of God and his football-playing mother, plus why he cannot regret time 'wasted' in the past as he relishes his latest Bundesliga role in the Elversberg miracle...
articles.body:
Now at Elversberg, the Texas-born forward marked his full Bundesliga debut with a goal in a 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen. He has since started in the 4-3 win at Borussia Monchengladbach. Only an offside flag denied him an equaliser against Bayern Munich.

"I went to celebrate and then when I turned around I was confused because I did not see any of my team-mates. It was an amazing feeling even though it did not count." Amazing is a word that he returns to often in explaining his emotions this past month.

And why not? Elversberg, this tiny German club playing in the top division for the first time, could not have been where he envisages his career kickstarting aged 20. But four games into the season and this young group of players are the talk of the Bundesliga.

"The expectation was actually quite the opposite of what we have already shown," says Campbell. "We are just giving everything that we have and trying to play the best football that we can." And that means playing without fear, taking the game to teams like Bayern.

"It is obviously a different level when you are playing against some of the best players in the world." But the key to it is "not to worry about who is standing there" and that has been evident in Elversberg's approach, epitomised by their enterprising forward play.

"Bravery for me as an offensive player is to not be afraid of going one against one and trying something instead of being scared and not trying it because of their reputation. Something we will continue to do is be brave, give 100 per cent and see what happens."

Speaking to Campbell, he sounds at home already. Asked who his friends are at the club and he name-checks most of the squad. "We are a very close team. I cannot say one guy." Elversberg even reminds him of Iceland, where he spent part of his childhood.

"There are definitely similarities," he says. "That small-town feel is similar to when I was in Iceland so I really like it here." He enjoys visiting the coffee shops and has a fondness for schnitzel. "But I cannot eat it so often because it is not the most healthy thing."

He has embraced life in Germany, learned the language too. "Before that, it was a bit difficult." Maybe his multi-cultural background helps. His mother is Rakel Karvelsson, the former Iceland international. "I can also train with her, which is fun," he reveals.

She still challenges him to the odd two-touch game. "She does not win anymore. When I was 14 or 15, I started to beat her." Campbell will not be following in her footsteps with Iceland though. He has declared for the United States instead. "That is set in stone." He was rewarded with a senior debut in the win over Canada this week.

What is not set in stone is how his career progresses and if it feels like an overstatement to suggest that Campbell was at a crossroads this summer, considering how difficult these past two years have been. It has been a waiting game for him after that initial breakthrough.

"I was expecting to play more," he concedes of his time at Hoffenheim. Five months yielded only five substitute appearances for the club. "Maybe someone else will look at it and say it was a waste for me." But Campbell himself refuses to see it that way.

"My mindset then was a lot different than it is now. The things that I have learned in these 22 months I would not have learned if things had happened differently." It was character building, then? "Without this then my character would not have changed."

Campbell adds: "Trusting in the plan that God has for you is something that you always have to do. God has a plan. I believe that it also strengthened my relationship with him and strengthened my mental toughness. I have become a better player."

These references to his religious beliefs are frequent throughout this 40-minute audience with a group of journalists from around the world. Asked about comparisons with Christian Pulisic, he says: "Comparison is the thief of joy. That is in The Bible."

On the subject of his Christianity, Campbell is at his most eloquent and it becomes clear that the process of rationalising this period in which his career plateaued was made manageable as a result of his faith. "It is very important to me," he explains.

"It is easy to get caught up in football and the things that surround it but in football there are so many ups and downs. It is a bumpy road, you are going to have lows. It's the same with life. To have God to hold onto in those times is something that kept me going.

"I can be the best footballer and achieve everything but in the end it means nothing if I do not have God by my side so my faith is everything for me. I want to tell people what I believe in and impact people in a positive way. For me, it is the most important thing."

Regardless, Campbell still needs to succeed as a player to have this platform. And so, particularly after the Hoffenheim experience, this move to Elversberg had to work. "I needed to get minutes for my career and to play a bigger role than what I had at Dortmund."

He adds: "The move for me was very important. And I think now, I am getting minutes, which is the most important for me to develop and to become the best player that I can be. This step in my career was the right one. And I am happy that I came here."

He is their record signing. "There is pressure that comes with it. But on the other hand, there is also a lot of trust from them to believe in me. And I would say that the pressure that I put on myself to perform was already there before the money was involved."

Campbell talks warmly of the atmosphere surrounding the football club and on a practical level can certainly be encouraged by how Nick Woltemade, Younes Ebnoutalib and Fisnik Asllani have all come to Elversberg and progressed their careers as a result.

"When you have other players that have gone there, they have gotten their minutes and they have developed and made a big step for themselves, that obviously it helps," he acknowledges. "It had an influence on me coming here. It was the right step."

Conversations with the club's hierarchy convinced him. "They explained their plan and what the club is about." And head coach Vincent Wagner is already proving a positive influence. "My defensive work is something that has improved a lot. He is helping me."

The challenge now, with Elversberg's support, is to become "the best version" of himself. "I do not think there is any right path. Every player is different." But this path is working for Cole Campbell, a United States international now and seizing his Bundesliga chance.

articles.title: England Women in World Cup 2027 play-offs: Lionesses have obligation to prove themselves after Spain disappointment
articles.summary: England must make it through two rounds of home and away ties to qualify for next summer's World Cup in Brazil; play-off campaign begins against Greece on Friday; Sarina Wiegman has begun to experiment with elements of her squad - that can only be a good thing for England's evolution
articles.body:
The Lionesses only missed out by a whisker, finishing their qualifying campaign with 15 points from a possible 18. Just one result away. But it's difficult to overlook how we got here. England's 4-0 defeat to Spain was an eye-opener, their biggest margin of loss for 17 years. The heaviest of Sarina Wiegman's time in charge.

It highlighted a gulf that felt more technical than tactical. In the moment, Spain showed themselves to be streets ahead in style and substance. A team with a plan, rooted in DNA and identity. Their possession-dominant performance blew England away.

The ignominy of the scoreline actually managed to flatter the losers rather than the other way around. And bigger picture, that poses a significant problem for Wiegman. Is a rivalry that was previously highly competitive now partial to Spanish supremacy?

The boss was at a loss to explain why England suffered for so long in a game that she expected to be "very tight". "What I'm trying to do now is think, what caused this?"

Hopefully by now, some of that soul searching has offered answers. Wiegman will be grateful not to have to prepare her side to play Spain on this ocassion, but Greece, a nation ranked 55 places below England in international status. The Lionesses are fierce favourites to progress across two legs.

Perhaps this window presents an opportunity, then. A chance to stress test England's resilience under pressure ahead of next year's World Cup tournament in Brazil. Clearly the most important outcome is getting there. But how they do it is relevant, too.

Those nations who consistently dominate international football are masters of reinvention. This is England's platform to prove themselves capable of that.

Wiegman has selected a squad of reliables mixed with a few wild cards, which will be welcome news to those critics (myself included) that believe England would benefit from an injection of fresh energy. Chloe Kelly and Ella Toone have been left behind . Chelsea's Lexi Potter has been named in her first senior squad. Captain Leah Williamson also returns after missing June's fixtures.

None of that constitutes a huge shake-up but is evidence of an intentioned move towards form-based decision making over reputational clout. In the thick of a World Cup cycle, that is the smartest play.

Potter is a precocious young talent who has thrived for Chelsea in a role alongside Keira Walsh this season. That pairing shows plenty of promise if Wiegman is looking for a tidy balance between ball winners and ball players in midfield. The boss believes Potter has already shown herself to be "comfortable" against top level opposition. Aston Villa's Lucia Kendall, 22, and 18-year-old Erica Meg Parkinson of North Carolina Courage are of similar ilk.

England's risk will of course have to be managed. They must accept these two games for what they are: must win. This next period is effectively their punishment for such severe underperformance in defeat to Spain three months ago. The reality of retribution.

And yet, the upshot might be beneficial. The Lionesses are clearly not World Cup ready and playing games of real consequence should help that. Ideally new faces stake a claim for a permanent place but it's equally important Wiegman's leaders turn up, too.

England's fear factor is built on their nucleus of world-beaters. Get Walsh pulling the strings, Lauren Hemp crashing down the wing and Lauren James firing worldies. Ask Williamson to be brave stepping out of defence. Lucy Bronze to take no prisoners. Alessia Russo to finish the move that tells the world England remain a creative force. Above all, be fearless.

While the other already-qualified European superpowers - France, Germany and Spain - watch on from their sofas, England must prove, beyond any doubt, that they deserve to join them.

England's path to next summer's tournament in Brazil is via two play-off rounds.

Round 1 takes place over two legs this month and is split into two paths. England are in path 1, drawn against Greece . They travel to Crete for the first leg at the Pankritio Stadium in Heraklion this Friday, before hosting at the King Power Stadium next Tuesday.

Round 2 is scheduled for late November. If successful, England will face the winners of Slovakia vs Ukraine , again with the away fixture played first.
